source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Sabey Ashburn Building A publishes 54 MW of IT capacity, the only figure on the record that bears on AI scaling, and it is a ceiling on draw rather than a statement of what is installed.

The certifications, SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001 and SSAE 18, qualify the campus for workloads with financial reporting controls, payment card data and protected health information. They say nothing about which tenants are actually there, and the operator does not publish that. No power source, utility, substation, cooling design, rack count or accelerator count appears at all.

Converting 54 MW into a physical footprint requires an assumption the operator does not make. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 54 MW is roughly 1,350 racks. At 10 kW per rack, typical of older enterprise halls, the same load is about 5,400 racks. Neither is Sabey's claim, and the real number depends on cooling and power distribution the record does not describe.

Within Virginia the campus ranks tenth among the 29 facilities in the state that publish a megawatt figure, against a published state total of 2,563.4 MW, or roughly 2 percent. Virginia has 376 mapped facilities and most publish no figure, so the 29 with numbers are a small and self-selected slice. The rank is real within that set and says nothing about the unpublished rest.
